info.title: Custom Objects
info.x-hubspot-api-use-case: After creating a Cars custom object, you can create a record for each car, then associate it with the contact who bought it.
info.x-hubspot-introduction: Use the objects API to create and manage records for an object. The endpoints can be used for objects included in all accounts, such as contacts and companies, as well as for custom objects in Enterprise accounts.

get.description: Read a page of objects of a specified type in your HubSpot account. You can control the data returned by specifying properties, associations, and whether to include archived records. This endpoint is useful for retrieving a list of CRM objects with specific details and associations.

parameters.name: objectType
parameters.description: The type of CRM object to retrieve, such as contacts, companies, or deals.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: A cursor token for pagination. Use the value from the previous response's paging.next.after field.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Whether to include archived records in the response. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: associations
parameters.description: A comma-separated list of object types to retrieve associated IDs for. If any specified associations do not exist, they will be ignored.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of results to display per page. Defaults to 10.

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: A comma-separated list of property names to include in the response. If any specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored.

parameters.name: propertiesWithHistory
parameters.description: A comma-separated list of properties to include in the response along with their history of previous values. If any specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored. Using this parameter reduces the maximum number of objects that can be read in a single request.

post.description: Create a CRM object with the specified properties and return a copy of the object, including its ID. This endpoint allows you to create standard objects in your CRM system, providing documentation and examples for guidance.

parameters.name: objectType
parameters.description: The type of CRM object to create, such as contacts, companies, or deals.

Location.description: URL of the newly created resource

post.description: Archive a batch of CRM objects identified by their IDs. This operation is useful for moving multiple objects to the recycling bin in one request, streamlining the process of managing large datasets.

parameters.name: objectType
parameters.description: The type of CRM object to archive, such as contacts, companies, or deals.

post.description: Create a batch of CRM objects for a specified object type in HubSpot. This endpoint allows you to create multiple objects in a single request, making it efficient for bulk operations. The response includes the created objects along with their IDs. This is useful for initializing large datasets or migrating data into HubSpot.

parameters.name: objectType
parameters.description: The type of CRM object to create in batch. This specifies the category of objects, such as contacts or deals, that the batch operation will apply to.

post.description: Retrieve a batch of CRM objects by their internal IDs or unique property values. This endpoint is useful for fetching multiple objects in a single request, which can help optimize performance and reduce the number of API calls needed. You can specify whether to include archived objects in the response.

parameters.name: objectType
parameters.description: The type of CRM object to read in batch, such as contacts, companies, or deals.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived. Defaults to false.

post.description: Update a batch of CRM objects in your HubSpot account. This endpoint allows you to modify multiple objects at once by providing their details in the request body. It is useful for making bulk updates to object properties efficiently.

parameters.name: objectType
parameters.description: The type of CRM object to update in batch, such as contacts, companies, or deals.

post.description: Create or update a batch of CRM objects by unique property values. This endpoint allows you to efficiently manage large sets of data by either creating new objects or updating existing ones based on unique identifiers. It is particularly useful for synchronizing data between systems or ensuring that your CRM data is up-to-date.

parameters.name: objectType
parameters.description: The type of CRM object to create or update in batch. This specifies the category of objects, such as contacts or deals, that the operation will target.

post.description: Permanently delete a contact and all associated content in compliance with GDPR. This endpoint can use the optional 'idProperty' set to 'email' to identify the contact by email address. If the email address is not found, it will be added to a blocklist to prevent future use.

parameters.name: objectType
parameters.description: The type of CRM object to be deleted, such as 'contacts'.

post.description: Merge two CRM objects of the same type into a single object. This operation is useful for consolidating duplicate records and ensuring data consistency. The request requires specifying the primary object and the object to be merged.

parameters.name: objectType
parameters.description: The type of the CRM object to be merged, such as contacts, companies, or deals.

post.description: Search CRM objects of a specified type using the provided search criteria. This endpoint allows you to filter and sort objects based on various properties, returning a collection of matching objects along with the total count.

parameters.name: objectType
parameters.description: The type of CRM object to search, such as contacts, companies, or deals.

get.description: Read an object identified by `objectId`. The `objectId` refers to the internal object ID by default, or optionally any unique property value as specified by the `idProperty` query parameter. You can control what is returned via the `properties` query parameter. This endpoint is useful for retrieving specific objects and their details from your HubSpot account.

parameters.name: objectId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the object to retrieve.

parameters.name: objectType
parameters.description: The type of the object to retrieve.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: associations
parameters.description: A comma-separated list of object types to retrieve associated IDs for. If any of the specified associations do not exist, they will be ignored.

parameters.name: idProperty
parameters.description: The name of a property whose values are unique for this object type.

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: A comma-separated list of the properties to be returned in the response. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored.

parameters.name: propertiesWithHistory
parameters.description: A comma-separated list of the properties to be returned along with their history of previous values. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored.

delete.description: Move an Object identified by `{objectId}` to the recycling bin. This operation effectively archives the specified object, making it inactive but not permanently deleting it from the system.

parameters.name: objectId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the object to be archived.

parameters.name: objectType
parameters.description: The type of the object to be archived.

patch.description: Perform a partial update of an object identified by `{objectId}` in the CRM. The `{objectId}` refers to the internal object ID by default, or any unique property value specified by the `idProperty` query parameter. Provided property values will overwrite existing values, while read-only and non-existent properties will be ignored. Properties can be cleared by passing an empty string.

parameters.name: objectId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the object to update.

parameters.name: objectType
parameters.description: The type of the object to update.

parameters.name: idProperty
parameters.description: The name of a property whose values are unique for this object type.
